guide.intro: Edebî İngilizce yoğun, çok katmanlı ve genellikle Latin kökenli kelimeleri Germanik kökenlilerle dengeler. C2 düzeyinde yazarın kayıt seçimi (Latinate vs Germanic), cümle uzunluğu ve metafor kullanımı kasıtlı bir araç haline gelir.

sections.text: İngilizcede aynı kavramı söylemenin iki yolu vardır: Anglosakson kökenli (kısa, somut) ve Latince/Fransızca kökenli (uzun, soyut). Edebî yazar bu seçimle metnin tonunu çevirir.

Düzyazıda anlatıcı seçimi (1. tekil, 3. tekil, serbest dolaylı, ikinci tekil) ton ve mesafe yaratır. 'Free indirect speech' (serbest dolaylı söyleyiş) İngilizcenin imzasıdır: karakterin düşüncesini doğrudan tırnaksız aktarır.

turns.text: So, what struck you about the prose? The narrator slips into free indirect speech without warning — did anyone find that disorienting?

lessons.title: Diyalog: Köşe yazısını editörle revize ederken
lessons.description: Bir gazetede köşe yazınızı editörle birlikte üzerinde çalışın — retorik figürler ve hedging.

turns.speaker: editor
turns.text: The argument's solid, but the lede is doing too much heavy lifting. You're asserting where you should be insinuating. Soften the verbs.

turns.speaker: you
turns.prompt: Editörün hedging önerisini kabul et
options: Fair point — I'll recast 'proves' as 'suggests' and let the reader do the arithmetic.
OK, I will make the words less strong, that is a fair point.
Sure, I'll dial down the rhetoric so it's not so in-your-face, totally.
turns.answer: Fair point — I'll recast 'proves' as 'suggests' and let the reader do the arithmetic.

turns.speaker: editor
turns.text: Better. Now, paragraph three — that tricolon. It's clean, but it lands as glib. Either earn it or cut it.

turns.speaker: you
turns.prompt: Retorik bir fiil — bir figürün hakkını vermek
turns.before: I take your point — let me see whether the tricolon
turns.after: its keep before I sacrifice it.
turns.answer: earns

turns.speaker: editor
turns.text: Good. And the kicker — you're hedging there in a way that reads as cowardice rather than nuance. Pick a side, or commit to your ambivalence.

turns.speaker: you
turns.prompt: Editörün eleştirisine yanıt verirken belirsizliği savun
options: I'd push back, gently — the ambivalence isn't a hedge, it's the argument. To resolve it would be to misrepresent the evidence.
I disagree with you, the not-deciding is the actual point of the piece.
Nah, that's me sitting on the fence on purpose, it's literally the whole point.
turns.answer: I'd push back, gently — the ambivalence isn't a hedge, it's the argument. To resolve it would be to misrepresent the evidence.

turns.speaker: editor
turns.text: Fair — though if that's the move, the kicker has to signal it. As written, it reads as flinching.

turns.speaker: you
turns.prompt: Retorik bir figürle yanıt — antithesis öner
options: Then let me rebuild it with an antithesis — 'not certainty, but the courage of uncertainty' — something to that effect.
I will make the ending have two opposite words to make it stronger.
I'll throw in some literary device, you know, like 'A but not A' or whatever.
turns.answer: Then let me rebuild it with an antithesis — 'not certainty, but the courage of uncertainty' — something to that effect.

turns.speaker: editor
turns.text: And the headline — it's serviceable, but it doesn't earn the piece beneath it. Can you give me something that whispers rather than shouts?

turns.speaker: you
turns.prompt: Hedging için yumuşak bir modal
turns.before: Let me try — something like 'Why the certainty is the symptom' — that
turns.answer: might

turns.speaker: editor
turns.text: Now you're cooking. Send me a fresh draft by six and we'll run it tomorrow.

guide.intro: Felsefe metni İngilizcenin en yoğun nominalleştirilmiş formudur. 'Olmak' ve 'bilmek' gibi temel fiiller isim haline gelir: being, knowing, becoming, awareness. C2 okuru bu yoğunluğu çözebilmelidir.

sections.text: Felsefede modal seçimi argümanın gücünü değiştirir. 'Might have done', 'could have done', 'may have done' arasında ince fark vardır: 'might' = en zayıf olasılık, 'could' = yetenek/imkan, 'may' = izin/ihtimal.

rows.translation: Böyle bir eylem sonuçsalcı zeminde savunulabilir olabilir.

rows.source: One ought not to assume that being entails knowing.
rows.translation: Var olmanın bilmeyi içerdiği varsayılmamalı.

sections.text: C2 sınavlarında felsefe metinleri sık kullanılır: yoğun nominalizasyon, hedge'lenmiş modal kullanımı ve uzun cümleli argüman yapısıdır.

turns.text: Let's begin from a deceptively simple question: when we say an agent could have done otherwise, what is the modal force of that 'could'?

turns.answer: I'd want to distinguish that from a weaker reading on which 'could' tracks merely epistemic possibility — what, for all we know, might have obtained.

turns.speaker: prof
turns.text: Good. And on the nomological reading, are we already conceding too much to the compatibilist? Rina?

turns.speaker: rina
turns.text: Possibly, yes — though I'd want to hear the counter-move before I commit.

turns.speaker: you
turns.prompt: Felsefi tartışmada modal bir yardımcı fiil

turns.answer: could

turns.speaker: prof

turns.speaker: you

turns.answer: The thought is that 'could have done otherwise' tracks something agential — a capacity exercised — and capacities aren't reducible to the modal profile of physical states.

guide.intro: C2'de şiir üretmek beklenmez ama tanımak beklenir. İngilizce vurgulu hece üzerine kurulu bir dildir; Türkçe değildir. Bu nedenle iambic pentameter (te-TUM × 5) bizim için 'tanıma seviyesinde' bir konudur. Ayrıca İncil ve Shakespeare cümleleri modern düzyazıda allüzyon olarak sürekli gezinir.

sections.text: İngilizcede her hecenin bir vurgu değeri vardır. 'iamb' = vurgusuz + vurgulu (te-TUM). 'pentameter' = beş iamb. 'Shall I compare thee to a summer's day?' = SHALL i com-PARE thee TO a SUM-mer's DAY. Türkçede vurgu daha eşittir; bu yüzden bu ölçüyü ÜRETMEK değil TANIMAK hedefimiz.

turns.speaker: ed
turns.text: Right, the manuscript's strong — stronger than the second draft suggested. But there are three things I'd like us to look at, and the first is structural.

turns.speaker: you
turns.prompt: Editörün yapısal eleştirisini açık şekilde davet et
options: Please — I'd rather have it bluntly. The pacing's been nagging at me since I finished, but I couldn't quite locate the problem.

turns.answer: Please — I'd rather have it bluntly. The pacing's been nagging at me since I finished, but I couldn't quite locate the problem.

turns.speaker: ed
turns.text: Chapters four through seven. The middle sags because you're protecting the protagonist from the consequences you've already set up. The reader senses the flinching.

turns.speaker: you
turns.prompt: Edebî bir öz-eleştiri fiili

turns.text: And the voice — it wavers in the dinner scene. You drop from your established register into something almost workshop-clean. Was that deliberate?

turns.speaker: you
turns.prompt: Editörün ses eleştirisine dürüstçe yanıt ver — C2 öz-farkındalığıyla
options: Honestly? No. That scene gave me trouble — I rewrote it eleven times and I think the eleventh draft is where the voice gave up.
Yes I did this on purpose because the scene is different.

turns.answer: Honestly? No. That scene gave me trouble — I rewrote it eleven times and I think the eleventh draft is where the voice gave up.

turns.speaker: ed
turns.text: Then let's rebuild it from the first draft. Trust the voice that got you here — the workshop instinct is the enemy.

turns.speaker: you

options: Understood. Give me three weeks for the structural and another two for the dinner scene — I'd rather come back with something cleaner than rush a half-fix.

turns.answer: Understood. Give me three weeks for the structural and another two for the dinner scene — I'd rather come back with something cleaner than rush a half-fix.

turns.speaker: ed
turns.text: One last thing — the epilogue. Drop it. The novel ends two pages earlier, on the image of the empty platform. The epilogue is you reassuring yourself.

turns.speaker: you
turns.prompt: Editörün epilog tavsiyesine yazar olarak yanıt ver
options: That stings — and you're right. I wrote it for me, not for the book. Consider it cut, though I'll mourn it briefly.

turns.speaker: ed
turns.text: Five weeks it is. And — for what it's worth — this is a real book. The rest is craft, and you've got that.
